brief: SEB's Q4 2026 themes note. A second summer energy-price surge ended central banks' patience with the shock: oil-linked inflation expectations jumped, repricing US rates from three cuts to 2.5 hikes by year-end and driving the rise in global yields; European gas sits at its highest since 2022, with relief unlikely before the 3 November US midterms as Iran has little incentive to ease pressure. Manufacturing has stayed resilient on an AI/defence/green-investment boom despite weaker services; September's PMI pickup in both hints at broader spillover. A likely Democratic House would gridlock Trump's fiscal agenda and risk blocking Fed appointments. France's deficit stagnation has pushed its swap spreads and France-Germany 10Y spread to the highest since 2012 ahead of April 2027's election, amid broader European right-wing gains. Japan's record intervention draws down Treasury-invested reserves, forcing a US dilemma between yen strength and Japan selling Treasuries; a hawkish BoJ would ease that. Warsh's Fed has turned hawkish despite pressure and wants a mandate regime change. Bessent's Treasury has turned activist, with buybacks read as an early yield-curve twist risking a USD-debasement narrative. China's surplus is redirecting toward Europe, raising EU-China tariff risk. Hyperscalers' AI capex is burning cash, shifting investor focus toward financing risk.
